subject: Escalation: HelioHealth multi-year pricing + renewal protection
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 15:07:00 -0700
Subject: Escalation: HelioHealth multi-year pricing + renewal protection

Hi Laura / Marissa / Aditya,

Following up from the commercial thread with HelioHealth — they're asking for a 3-year committed package and have asked for two non-standard protections: a price-lock for contract term and an "early-renewal protection" that limits uplift on any renewal executed within 180 days of term end. They also want an uplift cap of 5% year-over-year on list rates.

Why this matters: HelioHealth is committing to $3.2M ARR equivalent over 3 years (projected usage attached) and is moving a competitor workload onto Redwood if we accept these terms. This is strategic: references + potential marketplace case study. They also require a dedicated routing region (us-east) and SOC2 controls — legal & security are comfortable so long as we limit contractual exposure.

Ask: escalation to Deal Desk / Execs to approve:
- 3-year term with price-lock across the committed seat/throughput baseline
- renewal uplift cap: 5% absolute max per year; include an early-renewal protection clause (no uplift if renewed within 180 days)
- one-time onboarding credit of $30k to cover migration/prof services (to be applied in Q1)

Attachments: heliohealth-term-sheet-v3.pdf (term sheet w/ tracked changes), usage-commitment-forecast.xlsx

I believe this is within our risk tolerance given the size and reference value, but need explicit sign-off from Deal Desk and either Sales Exec or CFO for the onboarding credit. Can you advise by COB Monday 24 Aug?

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182

Attachment: usage-commitment-forecast.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Escalation: HelioHealth multi-year pricing + renewal protection

Stephanie — thanks for the context and attachments. Quick clarifying questions before we escalate to exec sign-off:

1) Baseline: confirm the committed baseline (QPS / tokens / reserved GPU hours) that will be protected under the price-lock. Is the attached forecast the committed baseline or expected usage?
2) Metrics: do we have an explicit overage mechanism (e.g., billed at list minus X%) if they exceed baseline?
3) Legal: I need confirmation from Legal on the exact renewal wording; can Legal provide a redline that limits evergreen exposure (no automatic rights to extended price-lock beyond committed baseline).

Conditional position from Deal Desk: I'm supportive of a 3-year price lock and an uplift cap for renewals tied to the committed baseline, but I want to tighten the uplift cap to 4% (instead of 5%) and require a usage banding clause (0-110% = protected; >110% triggers tiered pricing). Also, onboarding credit needs to be tied to a one-time success milestone (cutover + acceptance test).

Please send the committed baseline and I'll route to Legal for the renewal clause redline.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Deal Desk Manager | Redwood Inference

Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Escalation: HelioHealth multi-year pricing + renewal protection

Laura — thanks. Confirming committed baseline: 1,200 reserved GPU hours / month + 80M tokens/month baseline for pricing guard. The attached forecast is the committed baseline with a 12% expected step-up in year 3 (we included expected delta in the file).

Overage: customer agrees to tiered overage: 110-150% billed at list minus 15%; >150% billed at list. Legal has reviewed the renewal language and proposed the attached redline in the term sheet (see heliohealth-term-sheet-v3.pdf). Their ask is to make the early-renewal protection reciprocal: if HelioHealth renews early, they get the lower of then-current published rates or the agreed uplift cap — effectively preventing an increase if they choose to renew early.

I've pasted the key line in the redline: "If Customer elects to renew the Agreement within 180 days of the Term Expiration Date, the renewed rates shall be the lesser of (i) the Current Published Redwood List Rates at the time of renewal, and (ii) the rates calculated by applying the agreed annual uplift cap not to exceed 5% per contract year over the committed baseline."

Customer note: Priya is emphasizing predictability for procurement and is sensitive to multi-year inflation. They are willing to accept the usage banding and the milestone-based onboarding credit.

Attaching updated term sheet again.

Thanks,
Stephanie

Attachment: heliohealth-term-sheet-v3.pdf (application/pdf)
Attachment: usage-commitment-forecast.xlsx

Subject: Re: Escalation: HelioHealth multi-year pricing + renewal protection

Thanks for the updates — I reviewed the term sheet and usage forecast. Deal Desk position: APPROVE WITH CONDITIONS.

Conditions:
- Uplift cap to be set at 4% per year (instead of 5%) tied to committed baseline; include banding: 0-110% protected, 110-150% at list-15%, >150% at list.
- Early-renewal protection acceptable but must be limited to elective renewals signed within 180 days and only for the portion of baseline that is renewed (no retroactive extension to incremental capacity).
- Onboarding credit $30k accepted, but payable upon completion of cutover and acceptance test (milestone doc linked).
- Add explicit clause that year-over-year caps do not apply to pass-through third-party costs (cloud infra taxes / carrier fees).

Marissa, can you confirm exec approval for the $30k credit? Aditya / Markus, need your sign-off to finalize and send DocuSign. If we get sign-off today I will prepare the final DocuSign package and a cover note for Priya.

-Marissa
